subject: Unexpected embeddings ingest spike — reconciliation & EU VAT classification
messages:
From: Alexandra Ruiz <alex.ruiz@storify.co>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: finance@storify.co, t.kowalski@storify.eu
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sharp jump on July invoice — embeddings & ingest counts

Hi Irene,

Quick heads-up — our July invoice came in ~3x higher than expected (line item: embeddings ingest / "embed-ingest" token bucket). We ran a routine migration over the weekend to rehydrate an index, but our engineer believed the batch would be deduped by your ingest pipeline.

Attached is a screenshot of the bill and the invoice PDF (line 4). Can you help explain the sudden jump and whether this is billable? We're an EU B2B entity and would expect reverse-charge VAT treatment — the invoice currently shows VAT charged.

Thanks,
Alexandra
Alexandra Ruiz
Head of Data Platforms, Storify Inc.
[Attachment: storify_invoice_july2026.pdf (PDF, 68KB)]

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Alexandra Ruiz <alex.ruiz@storify.co>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp jump on July invoice — embeddings & ingest counts

Hi Alexandra — thanks for flagging and sorry for the surprise. We'll take a look immediately.

Quick ask to speed investigation: can you share the job id or timestamp for the backfill (approx start/end time), and ideally a sample of the IDs you re-ingested? If you don't have that handy, we'll pull server-side ingest logs and a per-request usage export.

I'll loop in Jordan (ops) and Ben (billing) — we'll aim to get a first-pass cause within 24 hours and propose remediation (credit/refund +/- VAT adjustment) as needed.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-10T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Embed ingest spike — preliminary findings

I pulled the per-request logs for Storify for the window 2026-07-24T22:00:00Z to 2026-07-25T04:00:00Z (their reported migration window).

What I see: a high-volume rehydration job started at 2026-07-25T00:07:12Z that issued repeated bulk embed ingest calls. Two things happened that compounded counts:
- The client retried with slightly different request IDs (no idempotency key), which bypassed dedup logic.
- A worker restart during the window caused temporary duplication of KV cache entries, so repeated streams resulted in double-counted tokenization events for ~47 minutes.

I've exported the request-level CSV and a short token-stream summary. See attachments (usage_export_aug09.csv, token_stream_sample.log). My rough delta estimate: ~2.1M additional embedding units (~$2.6k) attributed to duplicate ingestion.

Next steps: Ben, can you prepare a provisional credit calculation and advise on VAT treatment if we reverse-charge? Also, we should confirm with the customer whether the rehydration job intentionally retried without idempotency keys.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Service Reliability Engineer
[Attachment: usage_export_aug09.csv (CSV, 45KB)]

From: Alexandra Ruiz <alex.ruiz@storify.co>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: t.kowalski@storify.eu
Date: 2026-08-11T10:47:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Sharp jump on July invoice — embeddings & ingest counts

Thanks, Jordan / Irene.

We ran a one-off reindex during a migration and, yes, we retried on failure without idempotency because the rehydration tooling was a quick script. That was our mistake — apologies.

Attached is a signed VAT registration extract and a short log with a couple of job ids (job-44821, job-44822). We expect EU B2B reverse-charge treatment on the service; please let us know any evidence you need.

Appreciate your help here.

— Alex
Alexandra Ruiz
Head of Data Platforms, Storify Inc.
[Attachment: storify_vat_certificate.pdf (PDF, 12KB)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: billing@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed remediation: credit + VAT reversal (Storify / RDW-ENT-8731)

Team — based on Jordan's numbers and the customer's confirmation that the duplicate ingestion was accidental, I propose the following:

1) Issue a one-time credit for duplicate ingestion: USD 2,600 (calculated from 2.1M units at the customer's tier rate).
2) Reissue the July invoice with VAT reversed under EU reverse-charge (we need the VAT number and the signed VAT extract — which Alex attached).
3) If Alex prefers immediate refund instead of credit, finance can process a wire (I recommend credit to next invoice to avoid FX friction).

I've prepared a provisional credit note and an updated invoice PDF (proposed_credit_note_8731.pdf). I also added a short internal note about enabling stricter idempotency guidance in our onboarding docs to prevent recurrence.

If no objections, I'll: create the credit, update the invoice, and post the changes + ticket to HubSpot (RDW-ENT-8731).

-Ben Carter
Senior Billing Analyst, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_credit_note_8731.pdf (PDF, 9KB)]

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Alexandra Ruiz <alex.ruiz@storify.co>, t.kowalski@storify.eu
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, billing@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-13T14:03:00+02:00
Subject: Resolution: credit issued and VAT reclassification (Storify / RDW-ENT-8731)

Hi Alex / Tomasz —

Thanks again for the quick confirmation about the reindex. We issued the one-time credit for duplicate ingestion: USD 2,600. The July invoice has been reissued with VAT reversed under the EU reverse-charge rule (we used the VAT number you provided).

What to expect: the updated invoice (storify_invoice_july2026_reissued.pdf) is attached; the credit has been applied to your account as a line item and will offset the outstanding balance. If you prefer a refund, reply and we can request the wire (may take 3–5 business days).

As an operational follow-up, Jordan will send a short best-practices note on idempotency and we will add a short onboarding checkpoint about embedding backfills to prevent this class of duplication.

Ticket: HB-2026-8731 — I linked the HubSpot record and the usage export for your reference: https://hubspot.company/contacts/Storify-8731 and https://docs.redwood/usage/exports/2026-08-09/usage_export_aug09.csv

Apologies again for the disruption and glad we could resolve quickly.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192
[Attachment: storify_invoice_july2026_reissued.pdf (PDF, 70KB)]
